findings.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:198 — [P1, confidence 100] The unconditional `return false` rejects every SQL expression even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is globally enabled, leaving the new SQL command path unreachable.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1, confidence 100] The replacement database's `return "", errors.New("not implemented")` makes `TablesList` reject every SQL query before dependency discovery, so the removed DuckDB implementation leaves the advertised SQL framework nonfunctional.

pkg/expr/reader.go:129-131 — [P1; confidence 100] `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` followed by `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }` rejects every SQL expression because the helper has no true-return path, so the advertised SQL framework cannot construct an SQL command even when its global feature flag is enabled.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:13,17,21 — [P1; confidence 100] `return nil, errors.New("not implemented")`, `return "", errors.New("not implemented")`, and `return errors.New("not implemented")` leave parsing and frame execution unimplemented, so every SQL command fails instead of providing the task's analytics functionality.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-21 — [P2; confidence 100; advisory] The added public SQL DB surface consists solely of `errors.New("not implemented")` returns and the diff adds no tests, so regressions that leave all SQL creation and execution paths unusable reach users despite the plausible rebuttal that the feature gate protects them because the task introduces the framework rather than an intentionally disabled placeholder.

pkg/expr/reader.go:195 — [P1][100] `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` followed by `return false` forces the SQL-expression gate off for every flag state, so every SQL expression is rejected as unimplemented before command construction.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1][100] `return "", errors.New("not implemented")` replaces the removed DuckDB command runner with a permanent error, so `TablesList` rejects every nonempty SQL query and `QueryFramesInto` cannot execute one.

pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1; confidence 100] `return false` forces every SQL expression request to return "sqlExpressions is not implemented", replacing the Advanced SQL Analytics Framework objective with permanent feature disablement.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:15 — [P0, confidence 100; code: `return "", errors.New("not implemented")`] Replacing the SQL backend with an unconditional not-implemented error leaves the stated Advanced SQL Analytics Framework with no executable query path, so users receive no analytics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the enableSqlExpressions function at lines 193-199 in pkg/expr/reader.go. The function checks `!h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and assigns to `enabled`. If this is true (meaning the flag is NOT enabled), it returns false. But even if the flag IS enabled (making the condition false), the function still returns false at line 199. There is no code path that returns true, so SQL expressions will always be rejected with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error regardless of the feature flag state. This is a clear logic bug.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The feature gate in enableSqlExpressions() always returns false (the logic is inverted and both branches return false), which means SQL expressions are effectively disabled. The 'not implemented' stubs in db.go are intentional placeholders for a disabled feature, not a bug. The diff shows this is a deliberate removal of the go-duck dependency while keeping the interface structure, with the feature properly gated off. adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:195 — [P1][100] `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` followed by `return false` forces the SQL-expression gate off for every flag state, so every SQL expression is rejected as unimplemented before command construction.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the function `enableSqlExpressions` at line 193-200 in pkg/expr/reader.go. The logic is: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` which inverts the feature flag check, then `if enabled { return false }` and finally `return false`. This means: if the flag is enabled globally, `enabled` becomes `false`, the if-block is skipped, and it returns `false`. If the flag is disabled globally, `enabled` becomes `true`, enters the if-block, and returns `false`. In both cases, the function returns `false`, making SQL expressions always rejected as 'not implemented'. This is clearly a logic bug - the function should return `true` when the feature flag is enabled, not `false` in all cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — [P1][100] `return "", errors.New("not implemented")` replaces the removed DuckDB command runner with a permanent error, so `TablesList` rejects every nonempty SQL query and `QueryFramesInto` cannot execute one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the DuckDB dependency (github.com/scottlepp/go-duck) is being removed and replaced with stub implementations that always return 'not implemented' errors. However, this is intentional behavior - the reader.go changes show that SQL expressions are gated behind a feature flag (FlagSqlExpressions) and the enableSqlExpressions function always returns false, meaning SQL expressions are disabled. The stub implementations are placeholders for when the feature is properly implemented. This is not a bug but rather an incomplete feature that is explicitly disabled. The finding correctly identifies that the code won't work, but this appears to be by design as part of removing the dependency while keeping the code structure for future implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — [P1; confidence 100] `return false` forces every SQL expression request to return "sqlExpressions is not implemented", replacing the Advanced SQL Analytics Framework objective with permanent feature disablement.

adjudication.rationale: The function enableSqlExpressions() at line 191-198 always returns false regardless of the feature flag state. The logic is inverted: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` (negating the flag), then checks `if enabled { return false }`, and finally `return false` unconditionally. This means SQL expressions will never be enabled, and users will always get 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error at line 129. This is a clear logic bug that completely disables the SQL expressions feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the SQL functionality is being intentionally disabled/stubbed out. The new db.go file returns 'not implemented' errors, and reader.go adds enableSqlExpressions() which always returns false (the logic is inverted and both branches return false). This appears to be an intentional feature flag/disable pattern, not a bug.
